title: Splat / WorldModel: from wave packets to anchored worlds
summary: A split genealogy: layered atom tools, learned wave-manifold transport, observer-resource attacks, persistent field dynamics, and explicit world/provenance models. The pass also corrects an earlier false Splatworld2→WorldModel chronology.

nodes.claim: Interactive layered Gabor-atom sandbox with client-side loopy belief propagation, depth occlusion and explicit pose interventions.
nodes.survived: Object identity, occlusion uncertainty and user interventions are represented explicitly enough to make a practical layered scene editor.
nodes.killed: The repository does not by itself establish a new scene-learning theory; its GPU SDS path is separate from the verified browser inference core.

nodes.claim: Bet 8 plus a tested editing layer: atom erasure, template pruning, backdrop state and frequency-band gains.
nodes.survived: A useful separation between inference state, persistent template edits and render-only controls; erase/undo and gain identities are regression-tested.
nodes.killed: This is explicitly a client-side editing delta, not a new belief-propagation result; the inherited GPU SDS path remains unverified here.

nodes.claim: Turns the Gabor face decoder into a live avatar and tests whether complex packet phase carries the rendered field's motion.
nodes.survived: Phase-transport pursuit and a measured per-packet dispersion relation: rendered optical flow tracks phase rotation with slope about 0.998 and weighted r about 0.81 under a packet-pair scramble control.
nodes.killed: The encoder does not transport arbitrary input translation; out-of-manifold motion is re-indexed onto the learned face manifold. Patch phase-correlation also aliases badly on Gabor fringes.

nodes.claim: Adds persistent recurrent dynamics to a trained TinyAvatar/SplatWorld packet basis and solves the linear-regime loop spectrally.
nodes.survived: A real-spectrum loop law, distinct memory and responsiveness time constants, and a clean separation between external drive and autonomous continuation.
nodes.killed: Adjoint-symmetric autonomous dynamics cannot rotate; the first eigenmode-vs-eigenface metric was weak and failed its registered gate. Resolution detail cannot be invented by recurrence.

nodes.claim: Live predictive-coding loop that holds a Gabor-manifold belief and corrects it from sparse Lucas-Kanade flow, split into frequency octaves.
nodes.survived: Sparse observation can keep a rich latent belief attached to a stream; flow probes are more robust than color probes under lighting drift; the packet basis exposes a natural coarse-to-fine frequency decomposition.
nodes.killed: The loop does not acquire the correct world from nothing: an encoder/GIST anchor is still needed, and the face prior can confidently project a face onto inadequate input.

nodes.claim: After strong controls removed most 'splats as neurons' claims, the surviving object is an observer-resource frontier.
nodes.survived: When a task-relevant subspace aligns with a compact local observation vocabulary, one-time observer-description bits can buy a narrower repeated logical interface.
nodes.killed: Online branch growth, adaptive admission, Gabor-specific advantage, universal geometry advantage and a learned-observer-over-PCA headline are explicitly closed or not established.

nodes.claim: Separates addressed/topological coupling from metric/shared coupling and tests when slow shared metric history is useful.
nodes.survived: History can have an address vocabulary: in the constructed Gate 1 task, shared diffusive history helps only when useful context aligns with metric geometry.
nodes.killed: Gate 0 does not establish a special ephaptic computational advantage; a matched generic extra coupling solves the toy too. Metric state is not claimed to have unique capability.

nodes.claim: Inserts the ObjektiYksi operator-family construction in front of SplatWorld2's face-local rig: one stored material vector exposes many address-conditioned operators.
nodes.survived: One persistent material object produces a coherent address-conditioned transformation landscape; one conserved local edit deforms many addresses in a structured way without scrambling the whole landscape.
nodes.killed: The address coordinates are not learned camera/physical coordinates, the outer 'fire' is largely extrapolation/conditioning, and the plate is not established as a 3-D world.

nodes.claim: Moves the operator from camera space into a world-fixed splat field, then adds active inverse sensing of hidden material changes.
nodes.survived: Learned shared material beats its fixed-operator counterpart with far fewer trainable parameters than generic controls; active camera choice exposes missing material directions and improves local in-family inverse recovery.
nodes.killed: The learned operator is still less accurate than larger MLP/free-splat baselines; Gate 7A is only a positive control for small changes inside the same material family, not arbitrary scene understanding.

edges.why: SlapStack9 explicitly says it is Bet 8 plus a client-only editing layer and that the BP core/server files are unchanged.
SplatField explicitly starts from a trained TinyAvatar / SplatWorld checkpoint and joins persistent field dynamics onto the synthesis basis.
SplatField explicitly names a trained TinyAvatar / SplatWorld checkpoint as the basis for its stateful field.
TinyAvatar2 explicitly says its browser display follows SplatWorld2's anti-fire anchor rule and its face-dependent local-rig observation.
Splatworld3 explicitly nests the SplatWorld2 local transport basis under the new operator family and retains the old direct SplatWorld2 lineage.
Splatworld3 explicitly says it inserts the ObjektiYksi operator-family idea into the existing SplatWorld face manifold.
SplatWorld4 explicitly calls itself a fresh continuation of the SplatWorld operator experiments; exact gate-to-gate code descent is not claimed here.
SplatNeuronPlusField explicitly starts where SplatNeuron stops and names the old repo as the observer-resource project.
WorldModel's WorldSplat Studio branch explicitly lists SplatWorld as inherited compact learned-manifold machinery.
WorldModel explicitly inherits SplatField's separation of external drive from internal continuation.
WorldModel explicitly inherits TheSplat5's sparse-observation attachment of a rich latent belief and its warning about strong priors projecting the wrong world.
WorldModel explicitly inherits SplatNeuron's resource-currency accounting and strong-baseline discipline.
WorldModel explicitly inherits SplatNeuronPlusField's external-innovation versus recursive-projection distinction.

motifs.title: Transport can live in phase, not amplitude crossfade
motifs.description: SplatWorld exposes destructive additive interpolation as a failure mode; TinyAvatar turns complex phase rotation into a controllable transport mechanism; SplatField cites the resulting dispersion law as part of its medium.

motifs.title: A global manifold exposes different local rigs
motifs.description: SplatWorld2 measures identity-dependent local transport directions; TinyAvatar2 turns decoder Jacobians into manipulable local compliance and pin-driving structure.

motifs.title: External innovation is not recursive projection
motifs.description: The field/world line repeatedly separates new evidence from internally generated continuation so confidence cannot grow merely by replaying the model's own output.

motifs.title: Shared substrate plus active observability
motifs.description: One compact substrate generates many addressed responses; active sensing then chooses measurements that expose currently hidden directions.
